Harness.description: The program an agent runs on: `harness:` in its agent.md (`claude-code` is printed as claude), or a backup entry's. The host starts claude, codex, and any engine of the core's table with an ACP mode (`kith engines`); `agy` is the kernel's word for antigravity. One this version doesn't know is its own state: the host doesn't start it.

RolePrompt.description: How an engine takes the agent's role prompt, from the engine table's `enforces`: `flag` (a flag or ACP option on the command line), `env` (an environment variable), `first-message` (in front of the first message), `none` (not known to be deliverable: the host puts it in front of the first message). One this version doesn't know is read as none.

PermissionMode.description: The Claude Code permission mode a run starts in (kernel/lib/kith_settings.py CHOICES); a Codex run gets the host's translation. One this version doesn't know starts the run in default, which asks before every change.

DelegationState.description: Where a delegation (one `kith ask` id) stands: `open` (running, or parked on a card), `answered`, `capped` (answered, and its run took the chain to its cost cap) or `stopped` (the run gave no answer). One this version doesn't know is its own state: the host leaves it alone.

Agent.description: One agent in `kith ls --json`. `home` is its folder, where its bot works. A kernel from before `harness` was listed runs every agent on Claude. `builtin` is true for an agent that ships with kith (like scratch): never backed up or shared; older kernels leave it out.

NewAgent.description: `kith new <name> <description> --json`: the agent just made. `home` is its folder (memory, data and files beside the role), `dir` its role folder (its own repo: agent.md, settings.json, skills). A failure prints `{"ok": false, "error": "..."}` and exits non-zero instead, and leaves no folder behind.

Projects.description: `kith project ls --json`: every registered project, sorted by id.

Project.description: One registered project: its paths (absolute), its home folder when it has one, its git remotes, the project it sits in, its shared memory folder, and whether a folder of it is on this Mac.

Launch.description: `kith <agent> --launch-json`: how to start the agent, for claude and codex and, additively, any other engine the table lists with an ACP mode: `engine` is the table id (left out for claude and codex, which print what they always did), `acp` the installed CLI's own ACP program (null when it has none here: the host then starts the `registry` build), `role_prompt` how the engine takes `system_prompt`. `settings` is Claude Code's settings (null for another harness), `mcp_servers` its servers in Claude's format, `claude_args` the arguments `kith <agent>` would give claude (null for another harness). `backup`, `provider` and `account` say which backup entry, harness and login answer the run; `account_id` is that login as a backup id (`claude`, `claude:work`, `codex`), the agent's main account or the `--backup` entry.

AcpStart.description: How to start an engine over ACP, from the engine table (`kith kernel engines launch <id> --json`): the installed CLI's own ACP mode as a program. `env` is extra environment for it (the engine's keys are the host's own).

CostTag.description: What the cost ledger files a run's usage under. `via` is where the run came from (terminal, serve, a channel).

Delegations.description: `kith ask delegations --json`: every delegation record on this Mac, newest first.

Delegation.description: The record of one `kith ask` id (foreground, --bg or agent@machine), in kernel/bin/kith-ask's ~/.kith/live/ask/ID.reg. `agent` is the agent asked, `chain` the id of the root ask of its chain, `hop` its depth (0 at the root) and `cross_hops` how many asks of the chain crossed to another Mac. Money is in micro-dollars (US$1 = 1000000) at API prices; `cost_micro_usd` is null for an ask from before costs were kept. `cap_micro_usd` is the chain cap in force now (null: none). `capped_ms` is when this ask's run took its chain to that cap, and `cap_card_ms` when the host raised the Needs-you card for it (once per chain and cap). Times are ms. A record from before delegation records reads as a root ask: chain = its id, hop 0. `brief` is the ask's text (at most 2000 characters) and `session` the asked agent's session once a --bg run claimed one; both are for the owner's peek, null on an older record, and never part of a member's or bot's RPC.

Caller.description: Who asked: the agent (null for a terminal), the person whose run it is (null for the owner) and where it came from (`terminal`, `serve`, ...).

ReplyTo.description: Where the answer goes: the caller's session (a wake once nobody waits for it) and the ask whose run asked. This is the only place the address lives; cards never carry it.

KernelVersion.description: `kith kernel version`: the interface version and the modules this build answers.

Engines.description: `kith kernel engines --json`: the coding engines, installed or not, as the engine table describes them.

LaunchPrompt.description: `kith kernel launch prompt --json`: the system prompt a run gets.
